title: lot_multiple holds the LOT SIZE (107), and the design multiplies by it to state the minimum application
detail: The design says of field 49: "`lot_multiple` | 8 | DOC | BSE | - | keep | A3 | positive integer; `lot_multiple x lot x floor` is the true minimum" (§1.3), and §1.11 builds the SME rule on the same field: "Minimum application is **2 lots** (SEBI 2025), recorded in `ipo_details.lot_multiple`". The real extractor output contradicts it. `docs/design/probes/fixtures/extraction/asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd-PRICE_BAND_AD.json` emits `fields.lot_size = {value: 107}` AND `fields.lot_multiple = {value: 107}` - the same number, because the extractor is putting the lot size into the multiple. The ARCIL walkthrough confirms this reached production: `docs/design/walkthroughs/asset-reconstruction-2026-09-09.md:90` shows `lot_multiple = 107` stored today on a MAINBOARD IPO that is OPEN right now. Apply the design's own formula and the minimum application for ARCIL is 107 x 107 x 132 = Rs 15,12,468, when the true mainboard minimum is one lot at the cap, 107 x 139 = Rs 14,873 - a hundredfold overstatement of the number a retail reader uses to decide whether they can apply. The stated check, "positive integer", passes 107 without complaint. In Indian practice `lot_multiple` is 1 for a mainboard issue and 2 for an SME issue since the 2025 SEBI rule; it is never a share count.
where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.3 field 49, §1.11 (SME rows), Appendix A.1 row 49; evidence docs/design/probes/fixtures/extraction/asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd-PRICE_BAND_AD.json, docs/design/walkthroughs/asset-reconstruction-2026-09-09.md:90
recommendation: Give field 49 a real bound before any formula uses it: `lot_multiple IN (1,2)`, defaulting to 1 for MAINBOARD and 2 for SME issues that opened on or after the 2025 rule, and reject any value equal to `lot_size` as the known extractor confusion. Fix the extractor mapping in the same change (it is a distinct defect from the fresh/OFS ones in §2.5.4), and add a check that `lot_multiple != lot_size` on every row - it is the same share-count-in-the-wrong-column class the recurrence gate exists for. Until that lands, do not publish any minimum-investment figure derived from `lot_multiple`.

title: The Vinod Texworld walkthrough presents Asset Reconstruction's payload as Vinod's rank-1 source
detail: The walkthrough opens: "every value in the 'what the rank-1 source says' column is read from a payload saved under `docs/design/probes/fixtures/`. Nothing here is typed." (docs/design/walkthroughs/vinod-texworld-2026-09-09.md, header). It is read from a payload - the WRONG company's. Vinod Texworld is SME_NSE, listing_exchanges ["NSE"], issue size Rs 42.83 crore, stored lot_size 1200. Its rows nonetheless read `lot_size = 107` (line 45), `price_band_floor = 132` / `price_band_cap = 139` (lines 55-56), `lot_multiple = 107` (line 90), `designated_stock_exchange = NSE` (line 89), each citing `extraction/asset-reconstruction-company-india-ltd-PRICE_BAND_AD.json` - Asset Reconstruction's price band advertisement, a different, MAINBOARD issue. Vinod's own fixture (`vinod-texworld-ltd-DRHP.json`) returns `price_band_floor: null`, `price_band_cap: null`, `lot_size: null`, so those cells should read '(searched, no matching label)'. This is exactly the defect §2.3.4 says the design fixes - "A correct page still contains other companies' numbers" - reproduced inside the design's own evidence, and it is the class that publishes another company's price band on an IPO page. It also breaks OD-25 ('a claim cites a probe output or a saved payload'): ranks the fifth verification round counts as payload-backed for SME_NSE are backed by a mainboard company's payload. Second-order: line 45 shows source 107 against stored 1200 and grades the row `pass`, so the comparison column tolerates an eleven-fold disagreement between rank 1 and production without flagging it.
recommendation: Fix `walkthrough.mjs` to select fixtures by the IPO's own slug and fail loudly rather than falling back to any fixture that carries the field; regenerate both walkthroughs; re-count the 'payload-backed ranks' figure in §A.0's fifth round for SME_NSE, which is currently overstated. Add the same slug-binding assertion to the pull loop's evidence writer, and make the walkthrough's rule column report DISAGREES when the rank-1 value and the stored value differ, instead of `pass`.

title: The 30/90 anchor lock-in split does not exist before 1 April 2022, but the formula is unconditional and the 22:00 job walks backwards into those IPOs
detail: Appendix A.1 row 182 states: "computed: allotment_date + 30 days - SEBI ICDR 2018 Schedule XIII Part A, VERIFIED 2026-09-08 (50% locked 30 days from allotment, split rule for issues opening on or after 1 Apr 2022)", and row 183 the same for +90. §2.5.3's audit table then states the formula with no condition at all: "1-2 | `lock_in_50_percent_date`, `lock_in_remaining_date` | `allotment_date` + 30 / + 90 | **SEBI ICDR Sch. XIII Part A - verified**". The design has therefore recorded the effective date in the appendix and dropped it from the formula it will build. For any issue that opened before 1 April 2022 the SEBI (ICDR) Fourth Amendment 2021 does not apply: the whole anchor allotment was locked in for 30 days from allotment and there is NO 90-day tranche, so writing `allotment_date + 90` for those IPOs invents a lock-in expiry that never existed - on a date traders watch, which is §2.5.3's own reason for caring. §6.1 makes this reachable rather than theoretical: the 22:00 job picks "`status` is `LISTED` or `CLOSED`, and `close_date` is before today ... Ordered by `close_date` **descending**" with no lower bound, and §5.3 confirms pre-2023 rows are in that backlog ("a correct 2022 row would be rejected by a 2026 rule"). Separately, the citation itself is misquoted in the direction that matters for OD-25: §2.5.3 says "50% of an anchor's allotment is locked for 30 days from the date of allotment, the remaining 50% for 90 days", while Schedule XIII Part A as amended reads that fifty per cent of the shares allotted to anchor investors is locked in for NINETY days and the REMAINING fifty per cent for THIRTY days. The pair of dates is unaffected; the claim 'verified against the regulation' is not.
where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §2.5.3 (computed-field audit table, rows 1-2), Appendix A.1 rows 182-183, §6.1 (selection order), §5.3 (effective-date machinery)
recommendation: Move the anchor lock-in formula into the same effective-date machinery §5.3 built for validation rules: for issues opening before 2022-04-01 write one date (allotment + 30) and leave `lock_in_remaining_date` NULL with reason PRE_2022_NO_SPLIT; from 2022-04-01 write both. State the tranche mapping the way the regulation states it (the 90-day tranche is the 'fifty per cent'; the 30-day tranche is the 'remaining'), or rename the columns so the labels cannot be read backwards. This is not F-22 - F-22 is the bid-date-vs-allotment-date base; this is the cohort the split does not apply to at all.

title: The SME lot-value check is written two different ways, and the weaker one can never fire
detail: §1.2 row 4 states the check as "`lot x floor >= Rs 10,000` mainboard; `>= Rs 1,00,000` SME (2 lots x Rs 50k floor, SEBI 2025)" - i.e. ONE lot must be worth at least Rs 1,00,000. §1.11 states the same check as "the lot-value check is `2 x lot x floor >= Rs 1,00,000`" - i.e. one lot need only be worth Rs 50,000. The two differ by a factor of two and an implementer will build one of them. The second is the one that cannot work: the design's own §2.6 says "an SME lot is about Rs 1,00,000-1,50,000" (line 1594), so `2 x lot x floor >= Rs 1,00,000` is satisfied by every real SME IPO with a 2x margin and would still pass a lot priced at half the exchange floor - a check that cannot fail is not a check. The mainboard side has the mirror problem: `lot x floor >= Rs 10,000` is one-sided, so a lot size wrong by 10x upward (Rs 1,50,000 per lot on a mainboard IPO) passes, and the SEBI minimum-application band for a mainboard issue is a RANGE of roughly Rs 10,000-15,000 evaluated at the cap of the price band, not an open-ended floor evaluated at the bottom. ARCIL, open today, is the worked example: 107 x 139 = Rs 14,873 at the cap sits inside the band; the design checks 107 x 132 = Rs 14,124 at the floor against a lower bound only.
where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.2 row 4 vs §1.11 (SME on BSE / SME on NSE rows); design's own SME lot range at §2.6
recommendation: Pick one statement and put it in the validation configuration once (§5.3), not in two prose tables. Recommended: per-lot, two-sided, at the CAP - mainboard `10,000 <= lot x cap <= 15,000`; SME `1,00,000 <= lot x cap <= 2,00,000` - and express the 2-lot minimum-application rule separately as `lot_multiple = 2` (see F-63) rather than folding it into the lot-value bound, which is what made the two statements diverge.

title: The SME 2-lot rule is stated with no effective date, and 167 SME IPOs on production predate it
detail: §1.11 states flatly: "Minimum application is **2 lots** (SEBI 2025), recorded in `ipo_details.lot_multiple`, so the lot-value check is `2 x lot x floor >= Rs 1,00,000`", applied to "SME on BSE | 106" and "SME on NSE | 61" - 167 production IPOs. §5.3 establishes exactly the machinery this needs and explains why: "The date range is load-bearing, and it is what closes F-10 ... `listing <= close + 3 working days` is right today and wrong for anything that listed before December 2023, when T+6 was the rule. Applied without effective dates to the closed-IPO backlog, a correct 2022 row would be rejected by a 2026 rule." The SME 2-lot rule is the same shape - it took effect with SEBI's 2025 SME framework, so the overwhelming majority of those 167 SME rows closed under a 1-lot minimum - yet it is the one rule in the inventory stated without its window, and §1.11 is the section an implementer will read. The 22:00 job (§6.1) walks that entire closed population.
where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.11 (SME on BSE, SME on NSE), §1.2 row 4, against §5.3's own effective-date rule and §6.1's selection
recommendation: Give the SME 2-lot rule a `valid_from` of the 2025 amendment's commencement date in the validation configuration, and have §1.11 quote the configured rule rather than restating it. Then sweep every rule in §1's Check column and mark each one either with a window or with 'no window - always true', so this is the last rule that reaches the backlog undated.

title: The allocation check has the QIB inequality the wrong way round, allows the categories not to add up, and can double-count anchor shares
detail: §1.3 field 50 states the check as: "QIB + NII + retail <= 100; book-built QIB >= 50 (>= 75 where the regulation is cited)". SEBI ICDR 2018 Regulation 32(1), for a book-built issue under Reg 6(1), reads the other way: NOT MORE THAN fifty per cent of the net offer to QIBs, NOT LESS THAN fifteen per cent to non-institutional investors, NOT LESS THAN thirty-five per cent to retail individual investors. Only the Reg 6(2) route (Reg 32(2)) makes QIB a floor at seventy-five per cent, with NII not more than fifteen and retail not more than ten. As written, `QIB >= 50` accepts a Reg 6(1) issue showing 65% QIB - a value the regulation forbids and a mis-extraction the check exists to catch - and never tests the retail 35% floor or the NII 15% floor at all, which is where a mis-parsed basis-of-allotment table actually goes wrong. `<= 100` compounds it: the three categories must exhaust the net offer, so a row summing to 70 (one category dropped in extraction) passes silently. Third, field 72 `ipo_details.anchor_shares_offered` is a separate stored field, but the anchor portion is carved OUT of the QIB portion under Schedule XIII, so any sum that adds field 72 to fields 67-69 double-counts it - and the design never says which convention the four fields use.
recommendation: Split the rule by route, keyed on field 54 `sebi_regulation_cited`: Reg 6(1) -> QIB <= 50, NII >= 15, retail >= 35; Reg 6(2) -> QIB >= 75, NII <= 15, retail <= 10; fixed-price -> its own split. Replace `<= 100` with `= 100 +/- 0.5` over the three net-offer categories. State in the field spec that `anchor_shares_offered` is a subset of `qib_shares_offered` and add `anchor <= qib` as its check, so the double-count cannot be introduced by the writer.

title: "No draft prospectus stage" is wrong for a follow-on offer, and A.2's zero-N/A count contradicts §1.11's own sentence
detail: §1.11 says of FPO: "The rule is written and not exercised: no draft prospectus stage, so rank 1 is the RHP or prospectus directly; everything else follows mainboard." A further public offer is made under the same public-issue chapter of SEBI ICDR 2018 as an IPO and a draft offer document IS filed with the Board (Reg 25/26); the only FPOs that skip it are those eligible for the fast-track route (Reg 155), which is a per-issue condition, not a property of the offering type. Building the FPO plan on 'there is no draft' means the DRHP that does arrive has no document-type rank, and §6.5's warning applies directly - "A re-extraction must resolve a **real document type**, or type ranking degrades to newest-write-wins and an old draft overwrites a final price band advertisement." The same sentence also contradicts Appendix A.2, which gives "FPO | 0 | 0 | 240" - zero fields N/A. By §1.11's own claim at least field 55 `promoter_group_transactions_since_drhp` must be N/A (§1.3 says it is "only meaningful when a DRHP preceded the RHP"), and field 51 `pre_ipo_placement` is meaningless for a company already listed. A.2 already warns FPO "is the least trustworthy column in this appendix"; the warning is not a substitute for the fix.
where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.11 (FPO row), Appendix A.2 (FPO row), against §1.3 field 55 and §6.5
recommendation: Rewrite the FPO row as: the draft offer document exists unless the issue is fast-track under Reg 155, so the document-type ladder is DRHP -> RHP -> PROSPECTUS exactly as mainboard, and a missing DRHP is NOT_PRINTED rather than NOT_APPLICABLE. Mark fields 51 and 55 N/A for FPO and regenerate A.2 so its FPO column stops claiming 240/240. Add a first-FPO acceptance step to the build sequence: the first row that arrives with `offering_type = FPO` is walked by hand before its page is published.

title: The design never says which of the two Indian meanings of 'OFS' the 19 production rows are, and A.2 grants them 205 fields the exchange mechanism does not have
detail: §1.11 says: "**OFS** | 19 | No fresh issue: field 35 is legitimately 0 and `issue_size = ofs_issue`. No objects of the offer (field 27 empty is correct). No DRHP stage." In Indian primary markets 'OFS' names two different things. (a) The offer-for-sale COMPONENT of a public issue - which is what field 36 `ipo_details.ofs_issue` measures, and which is a property of an IPO, not an offering type; §2.5.4 uses it in exactly that sense ("fresh Rs 600 mn + OFS 20,213,722 shares"). (b) The SEBI OFS-through-stock-exchange mechanism, by which promoters of an ALREADY LISTED company sell via a one- or two-day exchange auction: there is no offer document, no price band (a floor price only), no lot size, no anchor book, no registrar basis of allotment, no listing date, and settlement is on the exchange. The design reads as (b)-shaped in saying 'no DRHP stage' while ranking rank 1 as the document and, in Appendix A.2, granting "OFS | 19 | 35 | 205" - 205 resolvable fields including the price band, the anchor book, the lot and the allotment timetable, none of which the exchange OFS mechanism produces. A.2 itself notes "OFS and BUYBACK (20 IPOs) have never had a single provenance row written", so nothing has ever tested which reading is true. If those 19 rows are meaning (a) they are mis-typed and are IPOs; if they are meaning (b) the field plan is wrong for all 19.
where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.11 (OFS row), Appendix A.2 (OFS row), against §2.5.4's use of the same word and §1.3 field 36
recommendation: Resolve it with a probe before build item 1, not in prose: read the 19 rows' `offering_type`, `price_range_min/max`, `lot_size` and document set from production and state which meaning they carry. If they are exchange-mechanism OFS, mark the price-band, lot, anchor and allotment families N/A for the type and regenerate A.2; if they are IPOs with an OFS component, correct `offering_type` and let F-20's plan-rebuild rule pick them up. Either way, name the two meanings in the glossary so `offering_type = OFS` and `ipo_details.ofs_issue` are never read as the same fact.

title: The 10-working-day window check is a public-issue rule applied to 8 rights issues that are legitimately open far longer
detail: §1.2 row 6 states the check unconditionally: "`close >= open`; `close <= open + 10` working days". That bound is SEBI ICDR 2018 Reg 46 - a public issue's bid/offer period is at least three and at most ten working days including any extension on a price-band revision. It does not govern a rights issue, which is made under the rights-issue chapter and is customarily kept open for fifteen to thirty days; §1.11 already knows rights issues are structurally different ("No DRHP, no price band advertisement, no anchor round, no lot size in the IPO sense") but the date rule was not scoped with them in mind. There are 8 rights issues on production. Under §5.3's regime they would be rejected as failing a plausibility check that is correct for a class they are not in - the F-10 class the design says it closed, surviving in a rule whose Check cell carries no offering-type scope. §5.3 provides the escape ("the offering types and segments it applies to"); §1.2 does not use it.
where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.2 row 6 (close_date check), against §1.11 (Rights issue row) and §5.3
recommendation: Scope the rule in the validation configuration: `offering_type IN (IPO, FPO)` -> `3 <= working_days(open, close) <= 10`; `offering_type = RIGHTS` -> a calendar-days bound of roughly 7 to 30; NCD -> its own window from the prospectus. While auditing that rule, add the missing lower bound for public issues - the current check has none, so a one-day window passes.

title: A rights issue's record date and entitlement ratio are absent from the 240 fields and are not declared as a gap, unlike the equivalent NCD gap
detail: §1.11 handles the rights issue purely by subtraction - "Fields 93-109, 131-137 are `NOT_APPLICABLE`, not gaps" - and adds nothing. The two facts a rights-issue reader needs above all others are the RECORD DATE (you must hold the shares on that date to receive the entitlement) and the ENTITLEMENT RATIO (for example 3 rights shares for every 5 held), plus the rights-entitlement trading window on the exchange. None of the 240 fields in Appendix A.1 carries any of them, and §1.11 does not list them as missing. The design does exactly the right thing one row above, for NCD: "Its own prospectus is rank 1 for coupon, tenor and rating - **none of which we currently store**, which is a gap this design surfaces rather than closes." The same sentence is owed to rights issues; without it, 8 production rows get a page whose most important dates are structurally unreachable and nobody is told why.
where: docs/design/data-sourcing-pull-model.md §1.11 (Rights issue row) vs the NCD row directly below it; Appendix A.1 (no record-date or entitlement-ratio field among the 240)
recommendation: Add one sentence to the Rights issue row naming record date, entitlement ratio and the RE trading window as fields we do not store, with the letter of offer as rank 1 and the exchange rights-issue circular as rank 2 - the same treatment the NCD row already gets. Then either add the three columns in build item 1 (they are cheap and the class is 8 rows) or record the decision not to, so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight.
